channel.title: Haiti Explorer — Analyses
channel.description: Short analyses, one figure and one question at a time, drawn from Haiti Explorer data.

item.title: Port-au-Prince has 78 times more inhabitants per km² than the median commune
item.description: In 2024, Port-au-Prince holds 27,087 inhab./km². Haiti's median commune has 347.4 inhab./km²: the capital is 78 times denser. Of the 140 communes, 8 exceed 1,000 inhabitants per km², 6 of them in the Ouest department.

item.title: In half of the communes, more than one inhabitant in three is under 15
item.description: In 2024, the share of under-15s ranges from 22.4 % in Port-au-Prince to 42.5 % in Thomassique. The median commune has 35 %.

item.title: 8 communes are more than ten minutes' drive from a hospital
item.description: The median road travel time to the nearest hospital exceeds ten minutes in 8 communes, and five minutes in 25. The longest is recorded in Bombardopolis (21.6 min). Half of the communes are within 2.2 min.

item.title: Trees cover more than half of the territory in 52 communes
item.description: According to the European Space Agency's satellite observation (2021), trees cover more than 50% of the surface in 52 communes, and less than 10% in 11. The share ranges from 0.3 % in Desdunes to 90.2 % in Chambellan.

item.title: In one year, prices rose by 16.9 to 19.8% depending on the region
item.description: Over twelve months, IHSI's consumer price index rises by 16.9 % to 19.8 % across the 5 regions of its breakdown. The smallest rise is in the region of Cap-Haïtien, the largest in that of Croix-Des-Bouquets.

item.title: Since 1952, 86 of 140 communes have had an earthquake of magnitude 6 or more within 50 km
item.description: The USGS global catalogue records earthquakes of magnitude 6 or more within 50 km of a Haitian commune on 5 dates: 1952 (6.2, near Pestel), 1953 (6.1, near L'Asile), 1956 (6.2, near Bassin Bleu), 2010 (7.0, near Léogâne, followed by a 6.0 aftershock) and 2021 (7.2, near Petit Trou de Nippes). Together they put 86 communes within 50 km of a strong epicentre, 48 of them within 25 km.

item.title: Almost one person in two in Haiti lives without electricity, a situation unique in the Caribbean
item.description: In 2024, 53.9% of Haiti's population has access to electricity, according to the World Bank. In other words, 46.1% of the population goes without it.

item.title: Fewer than one person in two uses the Internet in Haiti, against nine in ten in the Dominican Republic
item.description: In 2024, 47.9% of Haiti's population used the Internet in the previous three months, according to the International Telecommunication Union as reported by the World Bank. In the Dominican Republic, the share is 91%.

item.title: Seven in ten people in Haiti lack basic sanitation
item.description: In 2024, 29.1% of Haiti's population has basic sanitation: improved toilets that are not shared with other households. This is the definition of the WHO-UNICEF Joint Programme, used by the World Bank.

item.title: In 2025, prices rose by 28.6% in Haiti, the steepest increase in the Caribbean
item.description: In 2025, Haiti's consumer price index rose by 28.6% over one year, according to the International Monetary Fund as reported by the World Bank.

item.title: Diaspora remittances amount to 16.9% of Haiti's GDP, the largest share in the Caribbean in 2024
item.description: In 2024, money sent by migrants to their families amounts to 16.9% of Haiti's gross domestic product, according to the World Bank. The share was 14.8% in 2015; it peaked at 22.5% in 2020.

item.title: On the same island, life expectancy is 8.8 years shorter in Haiti than in the Dominican Republic
item.description: In 2024, life expectancy at birth is 65.1 years in Haiti and 73.9 years in the Dominican Republic, according to the World Bank. The two countries share the same island and have roughly the same population: 11.9 and 11.5 million in 2025.

item.title: In 2015, 39 of 66 mayors were elected with less than a quarter of the vote
item.description: In the municipal elections of 25 October 2015, the slate elected to the town hall won less than 25% of valid votes in 39 of the 66 communes whose final results the CEP published, and less than a third in 51. None reached half the vote.

item.title: In 2006, blank and spoiled ballots ranged from 4.1% to 31.5% depending on the commune
item.description: In the first round of the 7 February 2006 presidential election, the share of blank and spoiled ballots ranges from 4.1% in Delmas to 31.5% in Beaumont, across the 107 communes whose summary was kept. The median commune is at 16.4%.
